founderSource.sourceCoverageMeaning: All twelve source sections preserved in private comparison. This shared manifest contains only vetted reusable directions; case-specific interpretations/consultation facts remain private exemplars, not global rules.

policies.direction: Poor lifestyle habits reduce Driver scores even when no symptoms are present, but less severely than when symptoms already exist.
Symptoms have the greatest influence, especially when they negatively affect daily life. Excellent habits help but must not conceal significant impairment.
Severe concerns with meaningful quality-of-life impact take priority over favorable averages.
Symptom-to-Driver ownership and overlap rules should be expanded through controlled calibration; do not duplicate one symptom as independent burden across Drivers.
Missing information should trigger targeted clarification and potentially future questionnaire improvements, not invented scores.
Overall Health Spectrum classification prioritizes the strongest evidence of negative daily-life impact.
Action priorities balance symptom severity and ease of improvement.
